newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-United Int'l postpones Asia issues.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-United Int'l postpones Asia issues.

text.p: United International Holdings (UIH) Inc said on Thursday its subsidiary UIH Asia/Pacific Communications Inc (UAP) had postponed its proposed US$100 million initial public offering of class A common stock because of poor market conditions.
UIH said UAP had also postponed a planned offering of US$150 million of new senior discount notes by UIH Asia/Pacific Inc, a subsidiary of UAP.

"The public markets for UAP's proposed equity and debt transactions are not as strong as we expected and we have been advised by our U.S. underwriters (Donaldson, Lufkin and Jenrette, Merril Lynch and Smith Barney) to postpone our offerings for now," UAP chief executive and president Mike Fries said in a statement issued from Denver, Colorado and faxed to Sydney.

"We feel it important to point out that all of our operations in the Asia/Pacific market are peforming well and we are particularly pleased with the growth in our Australian multi-channel television business which surpassed 100,000 subscribers in December and continues to grow rapidly," Fries said.
"With cash on hand, and with UIH's support, UAP will have sufficient funds to continue the rollout of its businesses," he said.

"We also have been in active discussions with commercial banks and other financial institutions, who have indicated an interest in financing our core operations in the Asia/Pacific region and we will continue to monitor the public markets."
UIH has a substantial stake in Australis Media Ltd, Australia's first pay television operator.
UAP also has operations in New Zealand, the Philippines and French Polynesia which at November 30 had an aggregate of 1.6 million serviceable homes and 140,035 subscribers.
